content.value_statement: TypeScript projects need consistent rules for safe, maintainable code. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical guidance for strict typing, reviews, tests, and documentation.
actual_capabilities: Guides use of strict TypeScript settings and safer null handling patterns.
Recommends pnpm commands for formatting, linting, type checking, and test coverage.
Defines review checklist items for public API documentation and type safety.
Shows examples for typed errors, Result types, async functions, and type guards.
Highlights React performance practices such as memoization and lazy loading.
Discourages any, implicit any, excessive assertions, CommonJS imports, npm, and yarn.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not enforce rules without project tooling.
It assumes pnpm is the correct package manager for the project.
It does not include custom ESLint, tsconfig, or test runner configuration files.
It provides examples, not a full TypeScript curriculum.

use_cases.title: Review a TypeScript Pull Request
use_cases.description: Check changed files for strict typing, clear public APIs, safer error handling, and avoidable anti-patterns.

use_cases.title: Set Up Project Quality Checks
use_cases.description: Apply a pnpm workflow for formatting, linting, type checking, and running tests with coverage.

use_cases.title: Improve API Type Design
use_cases.description: Use unions, generics, utility types, type guards, and TSDoc where they make exported code clearer.

prompt_templates.title: Check Basic TypeScript Quality
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one file or small change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this TypeScript change for strict typing, null handling, and any avoidable use of any.

prompt_templates.title: Apply the Review Checklist
prompt_templates.scenario: Structured review before opening a pull request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the TypeScript quality checklist on these changed files and report only issues that need action.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Public API Types
prompt_templates.scenario: Refining exported functions, classes, or interfaces.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these public TypeScript APIs for clear types, useful generics, TSDoc needs, and excessive assertions.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a React TypeScript Module
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of typed React code and performance patterns.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this React TypeScript module for type safety, avoidable re-renders, lazy loading opportunities, and maintainable async error handling.

output_examples.input: Review a TypeScript service file before a pull request.
output: Flags one implicit any parameter and suggests a generic constraint.
Recommends a Result type for a function that currently throws mixed errors.
Notes that exported functions need TSDoc only where the signature is not self-explanatory.

output_examples.input: Set up quality checks for a new TypeScript project.
output: Recommends pnpm format, lint, type check, and test coverage commands.
Confirms strict mode should be enabled in tsconfig.
Lists review checks for no any, safer null handling, and ES module imports.
Suggests memoization only for expensive components or stable callback needs.
Recommends type-only imports for shared type definitions.
Identifies excessive type assertions and replaces them with type guards.

best_practices: Run formatting, linting, type checks, and tests before considering a TypeScript change complete.
Prefer clear inferred types, explicit public APIs, and type guards over broad assertions.
Use TSDoc for exported APIs when the intent is not clear from the signature.
anti_patterns: Do not use any or implicit any in production TypeScript code.
Do not replace clear types with excessive type assertions.
Do not use npm, yarn, or CommonJS imports when this skill expects pnpm and ES modules.

faq.question: Does this skill modify code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It gives guidance that Claude, Codex, or Claude Code can apply when editing or reviewing TypeScript files.

faq.question: Which package manager does it expect?
faq.answer: It expects pnpm and explicitly discourages npm and yarn for this workflow.

faq.question: Does it require strict TypeScript mode?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance expects strict mode in tsconfig and discourages unsafe typing shortcuts.

faq.question: Can it help with React code?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes React performance tips for memoization, callbacks, memoized values, and lazy loading.

faq.question: Does every function need TSDoc?
faq.answer: No. It recommends TSDoc for public APIs when the signature does not make the intent clear.

faq.question: Why were security findings dismissed?
faq.answer: The flagged patterns were Markdown formatting, documentation examples, and a relative API example, not executable malicious logic.
